text:
Sam: Heads-up — after rolling the new base image (nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12) to the us-west GPU pool a bunch of training pods report GPUs missing. Containers start but nvidia-smi shows driver comms errors.

Priya: Observed on ~40 nodes in us-west-2 canary ring, roughly 15% of the pool. Jobs error out at container startup with: `NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver.`

Marco: Any host-side kernel or driver bumps this week? kubelet restarts?

Sam: No kernel or driver changes on hosts — only change was swapping base image to include toolkit 1.12. The toolkit change seems to have altered mount behavior for /var/lib/nvidia and the libcuda symlink.

Jia: Can you paste the container start logs + `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ | grep nvidia` from an affected pod?

Sam: Paste from a failing pod: 
```
container_start: failed to load /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1: No such file or directory
/var/lib/nvidia: not mounted
host: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /dev/nvidia0 (broken)
```

Matt: That's interesting — toolkit 1.12 introduced different bind-propagation mode for the helper mount (HostToContainer vs private). If host-propagation is wrong, the driver device files don't propagate into the container. Could be a change to `--volume` flags in the entrypoint.

Priya: Reproducer (quick): `kubectl run -it --rm --gpus=all --restart=Never --image=redwood/base-gpu:toolkit-1-12 repro -- nvidia-smi` -> fails. If I switch to `redwood/base-gpu:toolkit-1-11` same node, works.

Marco: Can we confirm it's a mount propagation issue? Try exec into a running pod and `ls -l /dev | grep nvidia` and `mount | grep nvidia`.

Sam: From exec on failing pod: 
```
$ ls -l /dev | grep nvidia
# empty
$ mount | grep nvidia
# nothing
```

Jia: Host has devices: `ls -l /dev/nvidia*` shows the expected nodes. So root cause: container mount didn't bring /dev/nvidia or libcuda symlinks across.

Priya: Short-term workaround: pin base image to toolkit 1.11 for affected pools and redeploy. That fixes new pods. Also a manual `nsenter` + bind-mount into the container will recover existing ones. Not ideal though.

Matt: Longer term: update the helper that performs the bind mount to explicitly set `rshared` or `rslave` propagation when mounting `/var/lib/nvidia` and device nodes. The toolkit's wrapper may have changed default behavior.

Sam: Impact summary: ~200 job restarts in last 6h, higher tail latency for queued GPU work. No host reboots required. Canary ring only — not global, but autoscaler began scheduling extra spot capacity which increased cost.

Marco: Action items: 1) Priya - rollout immediate pin (1.11) to remaining us-west nodes (in progress). 2) Matt/Priya - prepare patched image that forces correct mount propagation and test in canary. 3) Ops - add alert for missing /dev/nvidia mounts at pod start to detect earlier. 4) Eng-runtime - coordinate rollback plan if mitigation fails.

Priya: Started pin rollout. Kicking off evict+drain on canary subset, should be done in ~30m.

Matt: I'll open a small PR to the entrypoint helper to force mount propagation and add a unit test for it. Also adding a comment linking to nvidia-container-toolkit changelog.

Jia: Please add a short postmortem note in incidents/once we have root cause confirmation. Might be worth checking dedicated/dedicated-gpu pool images too.

DeployBot: Canary rollout for base-image-toolkit-1.12 -> FAILED on 40/260 nodes with error: libnvidia-ml missing. Auto-paused.

OpsBot: Alert created: GPU_MOUNT_PROPAGATION_FAILURE_us-west-2 (severity: high). Affected pods: ~120.

Sam: If anyone finds additional reproducible host config that flips this (cgroups, containerd version, kernel mount flags) drop it here. For now pinning is lowest-risk.

Priya: Will follow up once pin rollout completes. If rollback needed we'll coordinate with SRE to throttle to limit cost impact. :thumbsup:
